Arg28 (reference residue, ARG in every contacting structure, none mutated) lies within 4.5 \u00c5 of an organic ligand in 32 of 39 ligand-bound structures. Inositol-phosphate-type ligands contact it: 4IP at 2.75 \u00c5 in 1BWN (4 of 6 instances) and 4PT at 2.58 \u00c5 in 2Z0P. Negative-control ligands never contacted it (3IS, 72V, A1JS1, IS7, MG, NYQ, Q1B, ZN). This matches the positively charged head-group site the hypothesis proposes. The refute criterion (no phosphate-like ligand within 4.5 \u00c5) was not met. Evidence: T1, E2, E3, E4 (E9-E11 are predictions only)."}, {"id": "H3", "verdict": "unchanged", "why": "Agent-generated hypothesis (stability/folding). T1 does not measure folding free energy, pLDDT or backbone dynamics, so it does not bear on this hypothesis. T2 (FoldX) is the test for it."}], "uncertainty": "T1 measures crystal-packing proximity to soluble ligands, not binding by the variant protein. No R28H structure is in the set. The four R28C structures (6TT2, 6TSE, 1BTK, 6YYF) show 0 contacts, but they carry no phosphate-type ligand, so that control cannot show a mutant effect. Most contacting ligands (about 28 of 32 structures) are synthetic A1B6x/A1JSx benzofuran compounds, so they are not evidence for inositol phosphate. The inositol-phosphate evidence rests on 1B55/1BWN (4IP) and 2Z0P (4PT). The contact is a distance threshold only; the atoms and whether the Arg28 side chain is the contacting group were not reported. The result cannot separate H2 from H1 or H3, which T1 does not test. Still needed: T3 (pocket and interface context) and T2 (stability), plus a laboratory binding measurement of Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 against wild-type and R28H PH domains."}
